uniform.focus: A constant state must stay constant to round-off. Any drift is an implementation error, not a method difference.

entropy.focus: Density advects diagonally with uniform B. Measures the hydro part only: the magnetic constraint is never tested.

alfven.focus: Circularly polarized Alfvén wave along x. Grid aligned, so ∇·B = 0 trivially for both methods.

alfven_oblique.focus: The same exact wave travelling along (1,2). Multidimensional induction: the first exact test where the two ∇·B treatments can differ.

brio_wu.focus: Coplanar shock tube, γ = 2. Grid aligned: compares wave resolution (compound wave, slow shock), not ∇·B control.

brio_wu_rotated.focus: Brio–Wu with the shock normal at 45°. The classic stress test: ∇·B errors appear at the discontinuities and corrupt the plateaus.

orszag_tang.focus: Interacting shocks form 2D MHD turbulence. Compared against the Athena++ 1024² reference at t = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5.

orszag_tang_3d.focus: Orszag–Tang with an out-of-plane velocity perturbation (ε = 0.2). No reference: compare morphology and energy exchange.

rotor.focus: A dense rotating disk winds up the field and launches torsional Alfvén waves. Look at the rotor shape and magnetic pressure.

current_sheet.focus: Two current sheets reconnect by numerical resistivity alone. Island count and magnetic energy loss measure dissipation.

field_loop.focus: A weak loop advects with vz = √5. Bz grows in proportion to vz·∇·B, so any Bz is a direct ∇·B error signal.

field_loop_novz.focus: The in-plane loop (vz = 0). Magnetic energy decay and loop symmetry after two crossings.

field_loop_3d.focus: A tilted cylinder of loops advected through a cube. Growth of the field component along the loop axis measures ∇·B errors.

blast_2d_b0.focus: Unmagnetized control: GLM and CT should agree up to their hydro differences.

blast_2d_b50.focus: Strongly magnetized cylindrical blast. Watch for negative pressures and the anisotropic shock shape.

blast_2d_b100.focus: β ≈ 2.5 × 10⁻⁴. Robustness test: count cells that needed the pressure floor.

blast_3d_b100.focus: The FLASH figure case, Bx = 100/√4π. Robustness and anisotropy.

decay.focus: Mach 2 decaying MHD turbulence, three seeds. Compare energy decay and spectra; no reference solution.

kh_uniform.focus: Double shear layer with a uniform weak field (β = 2×10⁵). Compare vortex growth and magnetic amplification; Tomida et al. found conventional Dedner stretched the vortices.

kh_localized.focus: Field confined to the lower shear layer. Field appearing at the upper layer before the layers mix is non-local ∇·B-error leakage (Tomida et al.: 10⁻⁴–10⁻² for Dedner).

kh_localized_dtjump.focus: The localized-field KH with dt divided by 40 for 100 steps at t = 3.0 (run to 3.2). GLM variants that tie c_h to 1/dt see c_h jump 40-fold, so ψ and ∇·B ripples jump; constant-c_h GLM (same kernel as the production path) and CT should not react.

decay_supersonic.focus: Mach 9, γ = 1.01, mean field 0.3 along z. Kinetic decay should agree across codes; magnetic energy and spectral bandwidth separate the methods.

throughput_ot3d.focus: Cell-updates per second and memory at 96³–384³, where the GLM production kernel can use its fastest tiles. Not an accuracy test.

gem.source: Birn et al. (2001) GEM challenge (MHD version)
gem.focus: Double Harris sheet with the GEM perturbation: an X-point forms and flux reconnects through each code's numerical resistivity (no Hall term, no explicit η). Reconnected flux vs Ωᵢt and the current sheet at the X-point separate the methods; the X-point is also where ∇·B cleaning is most stressed.
